title: Write Procedures People Can Execute and Audit

content.overview: A professional SOP is a controlled instruction for a defined task, not a collection of preferences. It states what the procedure covers, who is responsible, what must be ready, how work is performed, what is recorded and what happens when the expected process cannot be followed.

vocabulary.definition: A controlled standard operating procedure for performing a defined process consistently.
The process, location, material or role boundaries to which a procedure applies.
Evidence created to document what was actually done or observed.

sections.title: Separate requirements from explanation
sections.body: Procedure steps should be unambiguous and observable. Background science can be linked separately so required actions are not buried in narrative.

sections.title: Define roles and prerequisites
sections.body: Specify authorized roles, required training, tools, materials, safety prerequisites and forms before the first execution step.

sections.title: Design records with the procedure
sections.body: Every critical observation, decision or handoff should have a defined record location rather than relying on memory.

workedExamples: A cloning SOP should identify donor acceptance, sanitation, labeling, transfer steps and records instead of merely saying take healthy cuttings.
If an operator cannot tell what to do when a sensor is out of tolerance, the SOP is incomplete.
commonMistakes: Writing vague verbs such as manage or monitor with no acceptance criteria.
Mixing training notes into required procedure steps.
Adding forms after the SOP is already in use.
content.practicalApplication: Take one cultivation task and write purpose, scope, roles, prerequisites, ordered steps, records, exception/escalation route and references. Have another person follow it literally and identify ambiguities.
content.summary: Executable SOPs turn expected work into clear actions and evidence rather than informal tribal knowledge.
